title: Frequency Table

concept.title: A map that counts
body: The most common use of a hash map is **counting**: the key is the value you look at, the stored value is how often it occurred. For each element add one to its counter, starting from 0 when the key is new.
A hash map has no fixed order of its keys, so to print them in order you sort the keys first (or use an ordered map: `map` in C++, `TreeMap` in Java).

statement: Given `n` integers, print every different value together with the number of times it occurs, one value per line, in increasing order of the value.
outputFormat: For each different value, in increasing order, print the value and its count separated by a space.

examples.note: 1 occurs once, 3 twice and 5 three times.

hints: Use a map from a value to its count.
For every number add 1 to its entry (a missing entry counts as 0).
Sort the keys and print each key with its count.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: The map counts the occurrences of every value. Sorting the keys (or using an ordered map) gives the output order.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + d log d) for d different values, space O(d).
